newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch cabinet criticised over Maastricht airport.
newsitem.headline: Dutch cabinet criticised over Maastricht airport.

text.p: The Dutch cabinet was criticised for its decision to approve a limited expansion of Maastricht Aachen airport in a letter written last week by the ruling local council.

The Council of Beek, which has the airport in its juresdiction, said the decision, earlier this month to allow a small number of night flights and to give the airport a green light for a new runway is insufficient.

Local politicans are worried about an economic downturn in the region and have warned the Government that some 3,300 jobs in the area are directly tied to the success of Maastricht airport, the most southerly in the country.

The government gave the airport permission for two passenger charter aircraft to land every night. The airport's morning opening time for take offs and landings was extended by half-an-hour to 05.00 local time (04.00 GMT) every day.
But the airport was declined permission for airfreight flights to land at night, part of its original proposal.

A joint working group of Maastricht's management and a team from Amsterdam's Schiphol airport is studying the Government's decision, and is expected to report later this month. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
